name: Flour (wheat, corn, other — non-rice)

iAs.control: Inorganic arsenic does not hyperaccumulate in wheat, corn, or other non-rice cereals as it does in rice; no government sets an iAs ML for any non-rice grain or flour in any jurisdiction. This subcategory is the clean counterpart to the rice-based flour/pasta subcategories, where iAs is the binding Tier-1 analyte.
iAs.reference_method: iAs by HPLC-ICP-MS (EN 16802) on any lot flagged for arsenic screening; non-rice grain occurrence is characteristically < LOQ.

tHg.basis_note: HK Cap 132V grain total mercury 20 ug/kg (0.02 mg/kg; rice, husked/polished rice, maize, maize flour, wheat, wheat flour) — the strictest sovereign grain total-Hg limit; supersedes the looser Israel FCS-2016 cereals-and-cereal-products 30. The EU 2018/73 'cereals' 10 is a pesticide-residue MRL, not a contaminant ML, and is excluded.

MeHg.control: No government sets a methylmercury ML for any grain, cereal, or rice product in any jurisdiction; methylmercury maximum levels exist only for fish and seafood. Mercury in this matrix is controlled by the total-mercury ML (30 ug/kg, Israel FCS-2016), which bounds the methylmercury fraction. Rice can accumulate trace methylmercury via paddy-soil methylation in point-source-contaminated growing regions, but that fraction is bounded by the total-mercury control and no methylmercury ML exists to look up.
MeHg.reference_method: MeHg by GC-ICP-MS / EN 16801 only on a lot whose total mercury approaches the tHg ML; grain MeHg is characteristically < LOQ.

Cr.basis_note: China GB 2762-2022 Table 7 grains and milled-grain-products total chromium 1.0 mg/kg (total Cr, not Cr-VI); corroborated by HK Cap 132V Cereals Cr-total 1000.

Cr-VI.control: Cr(VI) (hexavalent chromium): reflex-speciation control on the total-chromium result (see the separate total-Cr cell, governed by China GB 2762-2022 grains/milled-grain-products total Cr 1.0 mg/kg). No jurisdiction sets a Cr(VI)-specific food maximum level; chromium in the cereal/rice matrix is dominated by nutritionally-essential Cr(III) and any Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in the matrix. Reflex control: any total-Cr result >= 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS; on any result >= 100 ug/kg, Cr(VI) by EN 15192 / EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope-dilution; LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.

Sn.control: Every government tin ML in the register is scoped to canned/tin-coated product; tin migrates from tinplate. Flour is not sold in tinplate, so tin is not a material contaminant. Canned grain products route to Category 7 and carry the tin flag there.

Al.control: No credible regulator sets an aluminium CONTAMINANT maximum level for grains, cereals, or rice products, and China GB 2762 (the contaminant standard) does not regulate aluminium. Aluminium present in leavened, baked, or alum-firmed grain products is permitted-additive residue (China GB 2760-2024 food-additive use limits, e.g. baked foods 100 mg/kg / starch noodles and vermicelli 200 mg/kg, calculated as Al), governed by additive ADI and the JECFA/EFSA provisional tolerable weekly intake, not by a per-food contaminant ML. An additive-use residue cap is not a contaminant government limit and is not published as one; background aluminium in plain grain is soil-derived. Managed by intake vs the TWI, not a lookup.
Al.reference_method: Managed by intake vs JECFA/EFSA TWI; periodic total-Al screen (ICP-MS); no per-food contaminant ML to look up.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, 8:1 basis, read-across)
